_comment: The shape of the ground, for building the real place. POINTS AT public elevation and hydrography products rather than embedding them, because a real DEM is far too large for a release bundle. Shape: schemas/locale.toml.

elevation_range.sampled_area: Bounding box 47.58 to 47.70 N, -122.75 to -122.62 W (the Silverdale area, about 10 km east-west by 13 km north-south)
elevation_range.method: Statistics computed over the box from the USGS 3DEP seamless elevation service (computeStatisticsHistograms) at approximately 10 m and 30 m sampling; both gave the same result to within 1 m.
elevation_range.note: Sea level in Dyes Inlet to about 178 m on the upland plateau. The town itself is low: the GNIS Silverdale point is 4.8 m (16 ft) and the Clear Creek mouth 2.8 m (9 ft), while the CDP centroid uphill is 15.7 m (51 ft) and Bucklin Hill is 69 m (227 ft).

regional_high_points.note: Sampled from USGS 3DEP at and around the GNIS summit coordinates; these are 3DEP-derived values, not published benchmark elevations.
regional_high_points.comment: The Gold Mountain-Green Mountain hills, about 12.6-12.7 km southwest of Silverdale, are the high ground of the Kitsap Peninsula and the one place USGS notes where older Pleistocene deposits and Tertiary bedrock are exposed away from the coastal bluffs.

elevation_products.project: WA_Olympic_Peninsula_Lidar_2017_B17 (also published as 'WA Olympic Peninsula 1A 2017' and 'C1 2017')
elevation_products.format: GeoTIFF, 10,000 x 10,000 m tiles, UTM / NAD83, bare-earth elevations
elevation_products.coverage_note: Covers the whole Silverdale area including the Green/Gold Mountain uplands (tile x51y527). This is the best product for this area and the one to use.

elevation_products.availability: NONE. The National Map returns zero topobathy products for this area, so there is no seamless land-to-seabed elevation surface for Dyes Inlet. Seamless 1-m DEM (S1M) also returns zero here.

shoreline_and_hydrography.dataset: NOAA NGS Continually Updated Shoreline Product (CUSP)
shoreline_and_hydrography.role: The NOAA shoreline dataset covering this coast.
shoreline_and_hydrography.method: Office interpretation of imagery or derived from lidar
shoreline_and_hydrography.use_constraints: Not for use in litigation; NOAA attribution requested
shoreline_and_hydrography.caveat: The InPort metadata record does not state which tidal datum the shoreline represents; NOAA's shoreline programme generally references mean high water, but that is not stated in this record.

shoreline_and_hydrography.dataset: USGS National Hydrography Dataset (NHD), best resolution
shoreline_and_hydrography.role: The USGS hydrography covering Dyes Inlet.
shoreline_and_hydrography.dyes_inlet_representation: Dyes Inlet is an NHDArea feature of FType 312 (Bay/Inlet). Adjacent NHDArea Bay/Inlet features: Chico Bay, Mud Bay, Ostrich Bay, Phinney Bay, Port Washington Narrows, Anderson Cove. The enclosing NHDWaterbody is Puget Sound, FType 493 (Estuary).

shoreline_and_hydrography.role: Successor to NHD; CONUS-wide coverage including this area, published as FileGDB and GeoPackage.

tidal_datums.note: Dyes Inlet has its own NOAA subordinate tide station, but NOAA publishes no datums for it; the datums below are from its reference station at Bremerton. Values are feet relative to Station Datum, epoch 1983-2001.
tidal_datums.practical_note: A great diurnal range of about 11.7 ft is large. Tide stage dominates both coastal flooding and tsunami outcomes here, and it governs shellfish and shoreline access.

named_features_for_orientation.note: All from the USGS Geographic Names Information System (GNIS), Washington domestic names file. Distances are from the GNIS Silverdale point.

water.name: Port Washington Narrows
water.note: The outlet connecting Dyes Inlet to Sinclair Inlet and the rest of Puget Sound.

streams.name: Clear Creek
streams.note: The creek through Silverdale; its delta is the low ground at the head of Dyes Inlet.

islands.name: Bainbridge Island
islands.note: Where the Seattle Fault's 923-924 CE uplift and fault scarps are best recorded.

surficial_geology_context.summary: Kitsap County lies near the centre of the Puget Lowland between Hood Canal and Puget Sound, land area about 1,020 km2, with about 338 km of saltwater coastline and 53 km of freshwater frontage. It is mantled by late Pleistocene glacial, glaciofluvial and glaciolacustrine deposits of the Vashon stade of the Fraser glaciation. Older Pleistocene deposits and Tertiary bedrock are exposed only along the lower parts of coastal bluffs and some valley flanks, with the exception of the Gold Mountain-Green Mountain hills. The landslide-critical stratigraphy is permeable Vashon advance outwash (Esperance-type sand) over the low-permeability Lawton Clay, which perches groundwater and drives bluff failure.
